questions.q: What keyboard shortcut converts a plain range into a real Excel Table?
options: Ctrl+T
Ctrl+Shift+T
Alt+T
Ctrl+F
questions.explain: Ctrl+T converts a selected range with headers into a real Excel Table object, first mentioned back in Lesson 1's shortcut list.

questions.q: What is the single most important practical advantage a Table has over a plain formatted range?
options: Formulas and formatting automatically extend to new rows added directly beneath the Table — no manual copy-down required
Tables can only ever hold text data
Tables cannot be sorted or filtered
Tables permanently lock the data so it cannot be edited
questions.explain: Auto-expansion is the real reason analysts use Tables: a new row added under the Table inherits every formula and formatting rule automatically, which a plain range never does.

questions.q: What does the structured reference Table1[Sales] mean?
options: The entire Sales column of Table1, and it stays correct as rows are added or removed
Only the first cell of the Sales column
A hardcoded reference to cell B2 that never updates
The name of the workbook file
questions.explain: Table1[Sales] refers to the whole Sales column by name and automatically adjusts as the Table grows or shrinks — unlike a fixed range like $B$2:$B$500.

questions.q: What does [@Sales] mean inside a calculated column of a Table?
options: The Sales value in the current row
The sum of the entire Sales column
The name of the Table itself
A reference to a different, unrelated Table
questions.explain: The @ symbol means 'this row' — [@Sales] refers to the Sales value in the same row as the formula, which is exactly what a calculated column needs.

questions.q: Why are structured references considered more reliable than plain cell-range formulas, not just more readable?
options: They automatically track the Table's actual boundaries, avoiding the classic mistake of a SUM range that silently excludes newly added rows
They calculate faster than any other formula type
They only work with numbers, never text
They require no header row at all
questions.explain: Because a structured reference points at the Table's actual, current column rather than a frozen cell range, it can't fall out of sync with the data the way $B$2:$B$500 can after new rows are added.
